parentMessage.title: You Don't Have To Figure This Out Alone
paragraphs: If you're feeling overwhelmed, confused, or just tired — that's okay. Most parents who walk through our door feel exactly the same way.
It's okay to have questions. It's okay to not know what's 'normal.' It's okay to want help without knowing where to start.
We're here for that. Dr. Sharuja listens first. She meets your child where they are — not where a textbook says they should be.
Progress looks different for every child. For some, it's writing their name. For others, it's tolerating a haircut, or joining a game on the playground. Every step counts.
You don't need a diagnosis to reach out. You don't need to have it all figured out. You just need to know something doesn't feel quite right — and that you want support.

parentWondering.title: Questions every parent carries quietly
parentWondering.description: You're not alone in thinking these things. Here are honest answers — from someone who's sat with hundreds of Mumbai families just like yours.

items.question: Why is my child struggling with everyday activities?
items.answer: Sometimes it's not effort — it's that their body or nervous system needs a little extra support. Getting dressed, sitting still, writing, or joining play can feel harder than they should. That's not your fault. And it's something we can work on together, gently.

items.question: Will my child be able to cope at school?
items.answer: Many children we see feel overwhelmed in classrooms long before anyone puts a label on it. With the right skills — and the right support at home — school can feel less scary. We help with the real things: sitting, writing, paying attention, making friends.

items.question: Am I doing enough?
items.answer: If you're here, you're already doing something important — you're paying attention. Parenting a child who needs extra support is exhausting. You don't have to have all the answers. You just need someone in your corner who gets it.

items.question: Will things get easier?
items.answer: Progress rarely looks like a straight line. Some weeks feel hard. Then suddenly your child buttons their shirt alone, or finishes homework without tears. We've seen it hundreds of times. Small steps add up — and you won't be walking them alone.

items.a: Pediatric occupational therapy helps children develop the skills needed for daily life — play, learning, self-care, and social participation. At Thrive With Sharuja in Kandivali West, Mumbai, Dr. Sharuja Sarap uses sensory-integrative, movement-based approaches tailored to each child's strengths.

items.q: Who needs occupational therapy for children?
items.a: Children from birth to 14 years who struggle with sensory processing, motor coordination, attention, handwriting, self-care routines, or school participation may benefit. A consultation helps determine whether OT is the right fit.

items.q: How does OT help children with autism?
items.a: OT supports sensory regulation, motor planning, daily routines, and social participation for children with ASD. Dr. Sharuja Sarap uses structured, play-led interventions that respect each child's unique communication and learning style.

items.q: Can OT reduce meltdowns in autistic children?
items.a: Many meltdowns stem from sensory overload or difficulty with transitions. OT identifies triggers and builds regulation strategies, often reducing frequency and intensity over time.

items.q: Can OT help children with ADHD?
items.a: Yes. OT addresses attention regulation, impulse control, executive function, and motor coordination — common challenges in ADHD that affect school and home life.

items.q: How is OT different from medication for ADHD?
items.a: Medication addresses neurological attention pathways. OT builds practical skills — organization, movement breaks, sensory strategies, and task completion — for daily functioning.

parentsReading.title: To the Parents Reading This...
paragraphs: Perhaps you've noticed your child struggling with things that appear effortless for other children. Maybe you've been told to "wait and see," while your heart tells you something doesn't feel quite right.
You may have spent countless hours searching for answers, attending appointments, reading reports, comparing milestones, or worrying about your child's future.
You may have wondered: "Will my child ever catch up?" "Will they make friends?" "Will they be independent?" "Will they be okay?"

As parents, these thoughts come from a place of deep love. And while every child's journey is different, one thing remains true—your child is so much more than a diagnosis, a report, or a list of challenges.

Behind every behavior is a child trying to communicate a need. Behind every struggle is a child with strengths waiting to be discovered. And behind every child is a parent doing the very best they can.

My role is not simply to provide therapy. It is to help families understand their child more deeply, celebrate progress that others may overlook, and create opportunities for growth, participation, and success.

Some victories may seem small to the outside world—a child trying a new food, joining a group activity, writing their name, tolerating a haircut, making eye contact, climbing a slide, or expressing a feeling.
But as parents, you know these moments are never small. They are milestones. They are breakthroughs. They are signs of progress.
You do not have to walk this journey alone.
Together, we focus not on what a child cannot do today, but on what they may achieve tomorrow—with support, understanding, patience, and belief in their potential.
Every child deserves to be understood. Every family deserves to be supported. And every journey deserves hope.

expertiseEcosystem.title: Expertise Ecosystem
expertiseEcosystem.subheading: Every child is unique. We use a combination of evidence-based approaches to support participation, confidence, independence, and everyday success.

movement-motor-development.title: Movement & Motor Development
movement-motor-development.explanation: From crawling and climbing to sitting at a desk and joining playground games — we help children build the strength, coordination, and body awareness that daily life quietly expects. Play-led, never pushy.

sensory-processing-regulation.title: Sensory Processing & Regulation
sensory-processing-regulation.explanation: When the world feels too loud, too scratchy, or too much — we help your child's nervous system find calm. Sensory integration isn't about fixing behaviour. It's about understanding what the body needs to feel safe and ready.

feeding-oral-motor-skills.title: Feeding & Oral Motor Skills
feeding-oral-motor-skills.explanation: Picky eating, gagging, or mealtime battles aren't always 'behaviour problems.' Often the mouth needs patient, playful preparation. We go at your child's pace — no forcing, no shame — so family meals can feel less stressful.

handwriting-learning-readiness.title: Handwriting & Learning Readiness
handwriting-learning-readiness.explanation: Messy handwriting isn't laziness. Often it's tired hands, weak grip, or a body that isn't ready to sit and write. We build foundations step by step — through play, not endless copying — so school tasks feel more possible.

aquatic-therapy.title: Aquatic Therapy
aquatic-therapy.explanation: In warm water, gravity softens and movement often feels possible for the first time. Children who avoid playgrounds or tire quickly on land frequently shine in the pool — supervised, playful, and always therapeutic.

reflex-integration.title: Reflex Integration
reflex-integration.explanation: Sometimes the body holds onto early reflex patterns that make sitting, writing, and calming down harder than they need to be. RMTI® and MNRI® help rebuild those foundations — gently, respectfully, and always at your child's pace.

parentIntro.title: A gentle place to start
parentIntro.description: You don't need every answer before you reach out. Here's how we think about therapy — in words that make sense at the kitchen table.
paragraphs: Every child is unique. Their therapy journey should be too.

The goal isn't to fix isolated skills on a checklist. It's to help your child participate more comfortably, confidently, and independently in the activities that matter most to your family.

For many children, yes. Movement feels freer and safer.
Absolutely. We've seen meaningful gains at every age we serve.

handwriting-difficulties.title: Handwriting Difficulties
handwriting-difficulties.reassurance: Legible, comfortable writing is possible. We've seen it happen many times.
handwriting-difficulties.intro: When your child hides their notebook or cries over homework, it's not laziness. Writing asks a lot of a developing body — grip, posture, patience, confidence. We build those pieces gently.
symptoms: Illegible writing despite practice
Complains of hand pain or fatigue
Refuses written homework
Teacher says 'careless' but you know they try
Can't finish tests in time
challenges: Tuition focused on content, not writing
therapyRole: Handwriting Without Tears — multisensory, not copying lines
Grip and posture fixes that stick
Hand strengthening through play
School accommodations during improvement
Ten minutes daily home practice — manageable
benefits: Readable writing teachers can mark fairly
Child willing to pick up a pencil again
handwriting-difficulties.whenToBegin: After age 7–8, if writing is still a battle, targeted help beats more worksheets.

faqs.q: Will more practice at home fix it?
faqs.a: Not if grip and motor foundations are wrong. We fix the root.

faqs.q: Is it too late for my 12-year-old?
faqs.a: No. Older children often improve quickly with the right approach.

faqs.q: Can they use a laptop instead?
faqs.a: Sometimes. We help you decide — and build skills either way.

attention-difficulties.title: Attention Difficulties
attention-difficulties.reassurance: Attention is a skill. It can be built, gently and steadily.
attention-difficulties.intro: Not every distracted child has ADHD. Some simply can't filter classroom noise, or their body needs movement before their brain can focus. We help without labels — just practical support.
symptoms: Drifts off mid-conversation or mid-task
Needs constant reminders for simple routines
Daydreams in class but sparks at home topics
Inconsistent — great one day, scattered the next
Restless when asked to sit and work
challenges: You repeat yourself until you're exhausted
Quiet kids overlooked because they're not disruptive
therapyRole: Attention profile and sensory check
Short movement routines before work
Timers, breaks, and desk setups
Gradual focus-building through engaging tasks
Teacher tips when you want them shared
benefits: Child learns what helps them focus
attention-difficulties.whenToBegin: Before gaps widen at school — whether or not anyone has used the word ADHD.

faqs.a: No. Any child whose focus affects daily life can benefit.

faqs.q: How fast will we see change?
faqs.a: Many families notice shifts in 4–8 weeks with consistency.
We'll talk honestly about routines — balance matters.

primitive-reflex-retention.title: Primitive Reflex Retention
primitive-reflex-retention.reassurance: These foundations can be strengthened — at any age.
primitive-reflex-retention.intro: Sometimes a child's body seems 'stuck' — poor posture, clumsiness, reading struggles — and no one can explain why. Retained early reflexes can be part of that story. Gentle movement can help the nervous system catch up.
symptoms: Slumps at the desk or W-sits on the floor
Clumsy despite practice
Reading or tracking feels harder than it should
Big reactions to small frustrations
Other therapies helped — but plateaued
challenges: Child tired of failing at new skills
Not sure what else to try
therapyRole: Reflex and movement assessment
Gentle RMTI and MNRI protocols in play
Home movements — minutes a day
Integrated with broader OT goals
Honest progress reviews
primitive-reflex-retention.whenToBegin: When progress has stalled elsewhere, it's worth asking if foundations need attention.

faqs.a: Yes. The nervous system remains adaptable up to 14.
Foundations shift gradually — often weeks to months.
Reflex integration is used worldwide in paediatric OT. Dr. Sharuja integrates it thoughtfully.

emotional-regulation-difficulties.title: Emotional Regulation Difficulties
emotional-regulation-difficulties.reassurance: Meltdowns aren't manipulation. They're a nervous system asking for help.
emotional-regulation-difficulties.intro: When meltdowns are bigger than the moment deserves — or recovery takes forever — your child isn't giving you a hard time. They're having a hard time. We teach regulation through play, movement, and connection.
symptoms: Explosive reactions to small changes
Long time to calm after upset
Frustration shuts down tasks quickly
Anxiety in new situations
You feel like you're walking on eggshells
challenges: You've tried discipline — it doesn't help
therapyRole: Understanding triggers — often sensory
Co-regulation strategies for you and your child
Movement and deep pressure that calm
Visual routines for predictability
School environments that support regulation
benefits: Tools your child can use — not just you
emotional-regulation-difficulties.whenToBegin: If emotions are shrinking your child's world, support early prevents anxiety and withdrawal.

faqs.a: Never. Regulation often has neurological roots. Seeking help is love.
Many children improve with OT strategies. We collaborate with doctors when needed.

faqs.q: How do you teach little kids?
faqs.a: Through play, movement, and visuals — never punishment.

school-readiness-concerns.title: School Readiness Concerns
school-readiness-concerns.reassurance: Readiness isn't a date on the calendar. It's skills — and we can build them together.
school-readiness-concerns.intro: School readiness isn't ABCs and 123s alone. It's sitting tolerance, pencil grip, following instructions, managing a uniform, and feeling brave enough to walk through the gate. We prepare the whole child — not just the workbook.
symptoms: Can't hold a pencil comfortably yet
Restless during table activities
Shy or overwhelmed in groups
Needs help with lunchbox, shoes, toilet
Anxious when you mention 'big school'
challenges: You want them to love learning — not fear it
therapyRole: School readiness check — play-based
Pre-writing and grip through HWT
Sitting stamina built gradually
Social play in small, safe steps
School visit advice and teacher notes
school-readiness-concerns.whenToBegin: Six to twelve months before school is ideal. Already in school and struggling? We can still help.

faqs.a: Around 3–4 for prep, or anytime concerns appear.
We build the body and brain readiness that makes academics possible.
Yes, when families need them.

down-syndrome.title: Down Syndrome
down-syndrome.reassurance: Progress looks different for every child. We honour every step.
down-syndrome.intro: Your child has strengths you see every day — warmth, humour, persistence. Therapy celebrates those while building muscle tone, hand skills, and independence for school and home. Every milestone matters.
symptoms: Low muscle tone affecting movement and posture
Fine motor tasks need extra help
Feeding or speech readiness challenges
Sensory preferences that affect daily life
Slower to dress, feed, or use tools independently

Mealtime and self-care taking extra time

Self-care broken into achievable steps
Feeding support when needed
Aquatic therapy for confidence in movement
Family coaching and school collaboration
down-syndrome.whenToBegin: From infancy is wonderful. Meaningful progress happens at every age.

faqs.a: Physio focuses on gross motor. OT on daily life — dressing, school, play.
Often brilliant for low tone. Fully supervised.
Always. Your team should talk to each other.

feeding-oral-motor-challenges.title: Feeding & Oral Motor Challenges
feeding-oral-motor-challenges.reassurance: Mealtimes can get easier. We've helped many families get there.
feeding-oral-motor-challenges.intro: If your child eats only five foods — or mealtimes end in tears — you're not alone. Feeding is one of the hardest parenting battles. We go slowly, without force, building skills and trust bite by bite.
symptoms: Extremely limited diet
Gags or refuses textures
Mealtimes last forever or end in battles
Distress with toothbrushing or utensils

Avoiding family meals and social eating
Pressure from relatives to 'just make them eat'

OPT exercises for strength and coordination
Sensory steps toward new foods
Responsive feeding coaching for parents
Coordination with your paediatrician
benefits: Parents with a plan — not guilt
feeding-oral-motor-challenges.whenToBegin: When feeding affects health, growth, or family peace — don't wait years hoping they'll grow out of it.

OPT builds oral foundations. We coordinate with speech teams.

social-participation-challenges.title: Social Participation Challenges
social-participation-challenges.reassurance: Social skills grow from feeling safe in your own body first.
social-participation-challenges.intro: Your child might want friends but not know how to start. Or group noise sends them retreating. Social struggle is often sensory, motor, or regulation — not personality flaws. We build the skills behind connection.

Anxious before playdates

Regulation tools for busy environments
Turn-taking and joint attention through games
Parent ideas for facilitating friendships
School support for group participation

You know how to support — not push
social-participation-challenges.whenToBegin: If social isolation is growing, early support prevents years of avoidance.

faqs.a: We work individually on foundations that make groups possible later.

fine-motor-challenges.title: Fine Motor Challenges
fine-motor-challenges.reassurance: Small muscles respond to patient, purposeful practice.
fine-motor-challenges.intro: When buttons won't button and pencils won't cooperate, your child may avoid tasks altogether. Hand skills grow through play — not shame. We make the small muscles strong enough for daily life.

gross-motor-difficulties.title: Gross Motor Difficulties
gross-motor-difficulties.reassurance: Physical confidence opens doors to play, sport, and belonging.
gross-motor-difficulties.intro: When your child sits out while others run, it's not lack of interest — often it's a body that hasn't found confidence yet. We build strength, balance, and bravery through play — and water when it helps.

conditionsList.title: Sometimes, You Just Know Something Feels Different
conditionsList.description: Sometimes the signs are obvious, and sometimes they're subtle. It may be difficulties with attention, emotional regulation, handwriting, coordination, sensory processing, learning, or simply a feeling that your child needs extra support. Whatever your concern, we're here to help you understand your child's needs and explore meaningful ways to support their participation and development.

servicesList.title: How we support growth and participation
servicesList.description: Eleven certified programmes — sensory integration, movement, handwriting, feeding, aquatic therapy, and more — woven into plans that fit your child's real life.
